methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $6M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Albacore is a Seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by John Huddleston and Dante Vaisbort. The company has raised $6.5M to date. The comparable universe consists of three private peers in adjacent maritime infrastructure and logistics segments (Standard Subsea, Clippership, and NetworkOcean); no direct public comparables exist in this emerging subsector.

Valuation analysis applies a stage-progression methodology, treating the $6.5M in total raised as a proxy for current fair value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement. This approach yields an implied valuation of $16M. The methodology is applicable given Albacore's clear stage positioning and the availability of empirical data on capital deployed.

The triangulation analysis, constrained by a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $14M (low) to $19M (high), with a median of $16M. The relatively narrow range reflects limited methodological diversity; a more robust conclusion would require additional comparable transaction data or revenue-based approaches, neither of which are presently available. Key uncertainties include the trajectory assumptions embedded in the stage-progression step-up and the representativeness of the three private peers. Additional information on Albacore's revenue runway, customer traction, or capital efficiency relative to the comp set would refine this estimate materially.
